news_and_events.heading: Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0
news_and_events.summary: Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, is organising the “Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0” on 23 May 2026 to honour outstanding Class 12 CGBSE students, including CG Top 10 Rankers and students scoring 80% and above.
news_and_events.content:
Honouring Class 12 Achievers of Chhattisgarh Through “Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0

Board exam results are a proud milestone for every student and family. Months of preparation, dedication, and hard work finally turn into marks that open doors to the future. 


To celebrate this achievement and recognise young talent, Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, is set to organise “Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0”, a special pre-result recognition event for Class 12 students across Chhattisgarh.


 


The ceremony will take place on 23rd May 2026, from 10:00 A.M. onwards, at the Auditorium, Kalinga University, Naya Raipur. Students who have performed exceptionally well in their Class 12 examinations will be invited to be part of this grand celebration of academic excellence.


Who Can Be Part of the Ceremony?


Students from the CGBSE board will be recognised under the following categories:



 CG Top 10 Rankers

 Students Scoring 80% and Above in Class 12



The event has become one of the most-awaited student recognition programs hosted by Kalinga University. Every year, it brings together meritorious students, proud parents, educators, and university leaders on one platform to celebrate success and inspire future aspirations.


Why This Event Matters


For many students, this is more than a felicitation ceremony. It is an opportunity to be recognised at one of the leading private universities in Central India. It is also a chance to visit the campus, interact with faculty members, understand scholarship opportunities, and explore higher education options after Class 12.


Kalinga University has built a strong reputation for quality education, career-oriented programs, modern infrastructure, and student-focused learning. With courses across Engineering, Management, Law, Pharmacy, Science, Arts, Design, Agriculture, and more, the university continues to support students in shaping successful careers.


A Proud Moment for Students and Parents


Scoring well in board exams deserves appreciation. Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0 has been created to honour that effort and encourage students to aim even higher in the next phase of life. It is a proud moment not only for students, but also for parents and teachers who supported them throughout the journey.


Register and Secure Your Spot


Eligible students are encouraged to confirm their participation and become part of this prestigious celebration at Kalinga University.


Toppers Felicitation Ceremony 5.0 and Kalinga University are both ready to welcome the next generation of achievers.

news_and_events.heading: One-Day Workshop
news_and_events.summary: The Central Library and Research Department of Kalinga University, in collaboration with Elsevier, organised a one-day workshop held in two different sessions.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: The Central Library and Research Department of Kalinga University, in collaboration with Elsevier, organised a one-day workshop - “From Trends to Transformation: Harnessing Scopus & Publishing Insights for Research Impact” in a hybrid mode. The workshop saw an active participation of 30 research scholars, faculty members, and professionals in person, and more than 70 participants joined online from all across India. The event was inaugurated by Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor of Kalinga University, who highlighted the University’s commitment towards research quality and publication visibility. The event was held in two sessions. In the 1st session, Dr. Nitin Ghosal, Ph.D., Customer Success Manager, South Asia, Elsevier, gave an in-depth overview of the Scopus database, navigation techniques, advanced search strategies, bibliometric data extraction, and effective research planning and collaboration. In the 2nd session, Dr. Abdul Azeez E. P., Assistant Professor, Vellore Institute of Technology, focused on publishing insights, academic writing, common causes of manuscript rejection, and the emerging role of AI in research.

news_and_events.heading: Legal Aid Cell Commemorates the 76th Year of the Indian Constitution
news_and_events.summary: To honour the spirit and values of the Indian Constitution, we celebrated the 76th Year of the Indian Constitution, which highlighted, i.e., justice, equality, liberty, and dignity.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: To honour the spirit and values of the Indian Constitution, our Legal Aid Cell of the Faculty of Law, the Faculty of Education, and NSS jointly organised and celebrated the 76th Year of the Indian Constitution. Themed "Dignity Beyond Text: POSH as an Instrument to Enforce Article 14 & 15 of the Constitution of India”, the event highlighted the principles of the Indian Constitution, i.e., justice, equality, liberty, and dignity. The commemoration began with a Welcome Address by Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor, followed by the Oath-Taking Ceremony. A major highlight of the day was the Inauguration of the Wall of Fame of Chief Justices of India, paying tribute to the Chief Justices for protecting our Constitutional values. Dr. Deepak Kumar Srivastava, Associate Professor, Dean & Registrar at Hidayatullah National Law University, Naya Raipur, delivered a speech on how the Constitution shapes social justice. The event also featured cultural performances that showcased India’s unity and diversity.

The Book Fair transformed the library into a lively hub, bringing book lovers together in one place. A major highlight was the “Author Interaction Session,” in which our faculty members who published their books shared their writing experiences. A total of six popular vendors were invited to the Book Fair, who showcased a wide range of books. This literary festival promoted knowledge and a culture of reading among students.

news_and_events.heading: National Seminar on Waste Optimization and Sustainable Practices
news_and_events.summary: The three-day National Seminar inspired participants to adopt sustainable practices for a cleaner and greener future and even promoted cross-cultural collaboration.
news_and_events.content: Under the auspices of AICTE-ATAL VAANI, we organised a three-day National Seminar on “Waste Optimisation and Sustainable Practices”: A Sustainable Approach to Solid and E-Waste Management, Energy Recovery, and Climate Change Mitigation.” Experts, researchers, students, and faculty members discussed solid and e-waste management, climate change mitigation, and energy recovery. The seminar promoted cross-cultural collaboration by featuring resource persons from Tamil Nadu. The inaugural speech was delivered by Chief Guest Dr. C.R. Prasanna, IAS, who delivered a speech on waste-to-wealth strategies. Guest of Honour Mr. Gurunanthan, IFS, mentioned sustainability policies, while other dignitaries shared their knowledge on cleaner technologies and energy recovery to seaweed-based reGuest cycling innovations. The seminar inspired participants to adopt sustainable practices for a cleaner and greener future.

news_and_events.heading: Role of Microorganisms in Plants and Human Health
news_and_events.summary: The session highlighted the impact of microorganisms on human health and the use of techniques like prebiotics, probiotics, biotechnological applications, antibiotic resistance, natural remedies, and more.
news_and_events.content: The Department of Microbiology and Botany of our Faculty of Science organised an online guest lecture on “Role of Microorganisms in Plants and Human Health”. The session was delivered by Dr. Chayanika Putatunda, Associate Professor (Microbiology) at Om Sterling Global University, Haryana. He explained that the impact of microorganisms is not limited only to digestion, but it also affects our bones, kidneys, liver, lungs, heart, brain, and reproductive organs. It can lead to some serious diseases like depression, heart problems, diabetes, obesity, or cancer. For this, she informed the attendees about modern techniques like prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and faecal microbiome transplantation as solutions. In the session, she also covered biotechnological applications of microbiology, the cleanliness of the Ganga River, the use of cyanobacteria, and indigenous remedies like the use of soil and turmeric. Organised by Dr. Faiz Baksh and Dr. Pradeep Kumar, the program was highly beneficial and informative.

news_and_events.heading: Guest Lecture on “Essential Narcotic Drugs
news_and_events.summary: The session highlighted the clinical importance of narcotic drugs in pain management and palliative care, and attendees were informed about proper usage and risks associated with misuse.
news_and_events.content: Our Faculty of Pharmacy organised a Guest Lecture on “Essential Narcotic Drugs: The Vigilance Needed for Safe Usage and Misuse Prevention”. The guest speaker was Dr. T. Pugazhenthan, Associate Professor, Faculty-in-Charge, Central Pharmacy & Essential Narcotics Officer, AIIMS Raipur, Chhattisgarh, who highlighted the clinical importance of narcotic drugs in pain management and palliative care. He informed the attendees about proper usage and risks associated with misuse. The session focused on regulatory compliance, national guidelines, and ethical responsibilities in drug handling. The program was successfully conducted under the guidance of Dr. Sandip Prasad Tiwari, Principal, Faculty of Pharmacy, Kalinga University.

news_and_events.heading: Judex 3.0 Moot Court Competition 2025-26
news_and_events.summary: The Judex 3.0 Human Rights Law Moot Court Competition 2025-26 featured Hon’ble Justice Gautam Chourdiya, who shared insights on the role of law in protecting human rights.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: Jointly organised by Surana & Surana International Attorneys and our Faculty of Law, the Judex 3.0 Human Rights Law Moot Court Competition 2025-26 featured Hon’ble Justice Gautam Chourdiya, who shared insights on the role of law in protecting human rights. Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor of Kalinga University, commenced the ceremony by welcoming all participants, while Dr. Azim Khan B. Pathan, Dean, Faculty of Law, highlighted the Faculty’s commitment towards legal excellence. Mr. Preetam Surana, Partner – Dispute Resolution and Head of Academic Initiatives, shared the vision behind JUDEX. Twenty teams from across India presented arguments on human rights issues, among which eight top-performing teams were selected for the quarter-final round. The entire competition was effectively managed by Prof. (Mrs.) Saloni Tyagi Shrivastava, HOD in charge, along with Ms. Paluck Sharma, Mrs. Darshi Sharma Guhey, and student coordinators, ensured smooth coordination.

news_and_events.heading: ICETSD 2025
news_and_events.summary: Our Faculty of Technology successfully organised a Two-Day International Conference on “Emerging Technology for Sustainable Development” (ICETSD) 2025.
news_and_events.content: Our Faculty of Technology successfully organised a Two-Day International Conference on “Emerging Technology for Sustainable Development” (ICETSD) 2025. It was in collaboration with Government Engineering College Raipur, Guru Ghasidas University Bilaspur, Visvesvaraya Group of Institutions Gautam Buddha Nagar, Ultra Tech Cement and Centre for Energy and Environmental Sustainability. Students, faculty members, researchers, industry experts, and policymakers explored the impact of emerging technologies on sustainable development. The Chief Guest of the event was Dr. S.P. Pandey, Advisor, Visvesvaraya Group of Institutions. The keynote speakers of the event were Dr. Sharad Chandra Srivastava, Professor and Dean, School of Engineering, Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya Bilaspur, who shared his thoughts on Industry 5.0, also known as Human-Tech Partnership, and Dr. Brijesh Patel, Research Professor, National Taiwan University, informed the participants on how new technologies are being used in Taiwan through social work and administrative actions. With over 550 participants, a total of 305 research papers were presented on different topics and a total of 7 technical sessions were conducted.

news_and_events.heading: International Conference (ICETSIMD) 2025
news_and_events.summary: The Faculty of Information Technology and the IPR Cell organised a Two-Day International Conference on “Emerging Technology for Sustainable Innovation Management and Development”.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: The Faculty of Information Technology and the IPR Cell organised a Two-Day International Conference on 'Emerging Technology for Sustainable Innovation Management and Development'. The chief guests were Mr. Ravi Singh, Abhanpur, Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor, Dr. Byju John, Director General, Dr. R. Udaya Kumar, Director of IPR Cell and Chairman of the conference Dr. O. P. Dewangan. Mr. Ravi Singh addressed in his speech that we should empower students with knowledge and skills to use existing technologies effectively. The Keynote speakers of the conference were Senior professors of Deakin University, Australia, Dr. Saman A. Gorji, Associate Professor of Mariano Marcos State University, Philippines, Dr. Erlin L. Gonzales, Associate Professor of Kamphaengphet Rajabhat University, Thailand and Dr. Khamphicha, Vice President, Kamphaengphet Rajabhat University, Thailand. There were various technical sessions conducted in which professors, academicians, and technology experts from India and abroad participated through a hybrid mode. Out of 1200 registered research scholars, a total of 319 research papers were selected, and 300 were presented in technical rounds. The event was well-coordinated by the students and faculty members of the IT department.

news_and_events.heading: Public Awareness Program on Groundwater Quality and Monitoring
news_and_events.summary: The event was organised to educate our students and local communities about the importance of sustainable groundwater management practices.
news_and_events.content: To educate our students and local communities about the importance of sustainable groundwater management practices, the Department of Zoology, in collaboration with the Central Groundwater Board (CGWB), Raipur, organised a Public Awareness Program on Groundwater Quality and Monitoring. Students and faculty members from Zoology, Botany, Biotechnology, and BBA participated in the program. To build engagement among participants, slogan-writing and extempore competitions were conducted on innovative ideas and powerful messages. The guests were Dr. Rajni Kant Sharma (Scientist-C, CGWB, NCCR, Raipur) and Dr. Priyanka Sonbarse (Scientist-D, CGWB, NCCR, Raipur), Senior Scientists from the Jal Shakti Department.

news_and_events.heading: Emerging Perspectives and Future Trends in Pharmaceuticals
news_and_events.summary: Our Faculty of Pharmacy successfully organised a Two-Day DST-SERB/ANRF, Govt. of India Sponsored International Conference to discuss advancements and challenges in the field of pharmaceuticals and allied sciences.
news_and_events.content: Our Faculty of Pharmacy successfully organised a Two-Day DST-SERB/ANRF, Govt. of India Sponsored International Conference on “Emerging Perspectives and Future Trends in Pharmaceuticals and Allied Sciences for Global Health and Well-being” under the guidance of Conference Convener and Principal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Dr. Sandip Prasad Tiwari. Students, researchers, and industry professionals participated in the discussions related to advancements and challenges in the field of pharmaceuticals and allied sciences. Various dignitaries from around the globe gave remarkable speeches on global healthcare, innovations and well-being. The conference welcomed 640 students as participants. Day 2 welcomed 20 participants in online oral presentations, 10 participants in offline oral presentations and 18 participants in poster presentations. Winners of the competitions were awarded with certificates and trophies. The conference was concluded by Dr. Sandip Prasad Tiwari, Convenor and Principal of the Faculty of Pharmacy, Kalinga University, with a vote of thanks to all the Chief Guests, Guest of Honours, Special Guests, Keynote Speakers, Esteemed Delegates and Participants for their presence to make this event successful.

news_and_events.heading: Health & Wellness through Ayurveda
news_and_events.summary: To raise awareness about Ayurveda, the Office of the Chief Proctor and the Faculty of Pharmacy organised a powerful discussion on “Health & Wellness through Ayurveda”.
news_and_events.content: To raise awareness about Ayurveda, the Office of the Chief Proctor and the Faculty of Pharmacy organised a powerful discussion on “Health & Wellness through Ayurveda”, presented by Dr. K. B. Srinivas Rao, a renowned Ayurveda Consultant and Panchkarma Specialist from Raipur. He addressed various misconceptions regarding Ayurvedic medicines and treatments of different diseases. He also explained its scientific principles and how it works effectively in disease prevention, along with other modern medical practices. Students and staff members actively participated in the discussion, and the event marked the University’s commitment towards holistic education and well-being.

news_and_events.heading: Kalinga University Clinches Gold at AIU Woodball
news_and_events.summary: Among 44 universities of India, our Woodball team secured a Gold Medal in the Mixed Double Event and a Bronze Medal in the Women’s Team Stroke category.
news_and_events.content: Among 44 universities of India, our Woodball team secured a Gold Medal in the Mixed Double Event and a Bronze Medal in the Women’s Team Stroke category, at the AIU Woodball Championship 2024-25, held at Parul University, Vadodara, Gujarat. Our athletes were accompanied by Dr. Sanjeev Kumar Yadav (Assistant Professor, Faculty of Physical Education) and Ms. Anamika Shukla (Assistant, Department of Sports), under the mentorship of Dr. D. Kalidoss, Director, Sports of Kalinga University. Their outstanding performance is proof of their hard work and exceptional sportsmanship.

news_and_events.heading: Two Days Global Conference On Recent Trends in Law
news_and_events.summary: Our Faculty of Law, in collaboration with several prestigious institutions, organised a Two-Day Global Conference which was attended by legal experts, policymakers, and academicians.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: Our Faculty of Law, in collaboration with several prestigious institutions, organised a Two-Day Global Conference on Recent Trends in Law, Arbitration, Mediation, Economy and Society, which was attended by legal experts, policymakers, and academicians. The welcome speech was given by Prof. (Dr.) Azimkhan B. Pathan, Dean, Faculty of Law, which was further carried on by Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor and Dr. Sandeep Gandhi, Registrar, Kalinga University. The keynote address was given by Hon’ble Justice Saleem Marsoof, Former Judge of the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, who presented a detailed analysis of global dispute resolution mechanisms, particularly focusing on arbitration and alternative dispute resolution (ADR). Adv. K. Riju Raj S. Jamwal, Advocate & Legal Consultant, Supreme Court of India and Managing Partner, JRD & Partners, highlighted the impact of artificial intelligence on the legal profession. Panel discussions formed an integral part of the event, covering topics such as the role of law and mediation in economic growth and social justice. The Vote of Thanks was delivered by Mrs. Saloni Tyagi Shrivastava, HOD, Faculty of Law, Kalinga University. The second day of the conference continued with technical sessions, research paper presentations, and interactive discussions. The conference saw the participation of 200 research paper presenters and 150 attendees, and Certificates of Merit were awarded to the top three best paper presentations.

news_and_events.heading: Hackathon-2025
news_and_events.summary: The Faculty of Information Technology successfully conducted the 24-hour KU Hackathon-2025 at its campus, bringing together 26 teams from six different states.
news_and_events.content:
About the Program: The Faculty of Information Technology successfully conducted the 24-hour KU Hackathon-2025 at its campus, bringing together 26 teams from six different states. The Chief Guest was Mr. Vinod Pande, Project Manager at Yasham Software Services and the Guest of Honour was Dr. Piyush Mehta, CEO of Foresight Edge Private Limited. Dr. Omprakash Dewangan, Head of the Department of CS and IT and Convener of the event, delivered the opening speech, followed by Dr. R. Shridhar, Vice-Chancellor of Kalinga University and Dr. Byju John, Director General of Kalinga University.


The winners were:


1st Prize (INR 10,000/-) – Team BW Zero Waste Pioneers (Hirak Ganguly & Ipsita Tanaya Phukan, Braneware University, Kolkata)


2nd Prize (INR 7,500/-) – Team Spartans (Amarjit Singh & Priyanshu Prasad, IIT Madras)


3rd Prize (INR 5,000/-) – Team Kavach (Arhasi Soni & Jasleen Kaur Matharoo, Amity University, Raipur)


The event was well-coordinated by Mr. Kamlesh Kumar Yadav, Assistant Professor, with support from other faculty members of the CS & IT department. The valedictory ceremony was graced by Chief Guest Dr. Sreejit Panicker, Training Head at Techment Technology Pvt. Ltd.

news_and_events.heading: Trainers’ Training Certification Course on the POSH Act, 2013
news_and_events.summary: The Faculty of Law, in collaboration with the Indian National Bar Association (INBA), organized Trainers’ Training Certification Course” to educate and train participants on the legal and practical aspects of sexual harassment in the workplace.
news_and_events.content: About the Program: The Faculty of Law, in collaboration with the Indian National Bar Association (INBA), organized Trainers’ Training Certification Course” on the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, 2013, aimed at educating and training participants on the legal and practical aspects of sexual harassment in the workplace. Held on every Saturday and Sunday via the Microsoft Teams platform, the training program saw an active participation of over 200 people from various sectors, including industry professionals, HR experts, and academicians. Participants were informed about employer accountability, the functioning of Internal Complaint Committees (ICC), and implementing communication strategies to address and prevent harassment. Mrs. Vinakshi Kadan Singh, Advocate at the Supreme Court, put emphasis on workplace equality, Ms. Neetika Bajaj, Advocate at the Delhi High Court, focused on the various forms of sexual harassment, Dr. Badrinath Srinivasan from Bharat Petroleum explained the role of the Internal Complaint Committee (ICC) and the legal framework surrounding POSH, and many other legal experts presented impactful sessions. This training program was an important step toward creating a safer and more inclusive work environment.

video_interviews.description: I really like that the IT curriculum here is updated according to the latest industry trends. We learn about modern technologies like AI, cloud computing, and data analytics, which are in high demand right now. The faculty also invites industry experts for guest lectures, which give us real-world insights. Because of this, I feel well-prepared for my future career in the IT industry.

The faculty members here are really very supportive. Whenever I had doubts, they were always ready to explain everything patiently, even outside class hours. They also guided me during my projects and helped me learn new technologies. Their mentorship gave me a clear idea about my career options in IT. Honestly, I feel lucky to have such helpful teachers.

Studying IT at Kalinga University has been a great experience for me. The best part is the practical exposure we get in the computer labs. We work on real projects, coding assignments, and the latest software tools, which improve our skills a lot. The faculty makes sure we understand every concept properly by showing us practical examples. I feel much more confident about my technical knowledge now.

I really like that the curriculum here is tailored to industry needs. We studied topics like financial analytics, business strategies, and digital marketing, which are in high demand today. The workshops, case studies, and simulations improved my problem-solving skills. I also learnt teamwork and leadership through group activities. This industry-focused approach has made me job-ready.

Studying commerce at Kalinga University provided me with extensive practical exposure. I have worked on live projects, industrial visits, and internship opportunities with reputed companies. These experiences helped me understand how businesses actually work in real life. The faculty consistently supported us during these activities and provided detailed explanations. I am now confident and well-prepared for my future career.

One thing I appreciate the most about the Faculty of Commerce & Management is the personal attention we get. The teachers always guide us individually whenever we face difficulties. They helped me improve my presentation, decision-making, and communication skills, and I have always received proper guidance for choosing the right career path. This personal support has boosted my confidence.

Studying Forensic Science at Kalinga University was the best decision of my life, as they frequently conduct workshops, seminars, and conferences, which provided me with networking opportunities and to work on real investigation cases. It even broadened my critical thinking abilities, and I even got to know about different career opportunities in this field.

The best part of studying science at Kalinga University is their lab facilities, and I must say their labs have the most advanced equipment, which helped me a lot in the experimentation work. For me, every lab session was a completely new experience, and even the professors guided me on how to use the instruments and record results.

I opted for a B.Sc. in Biotechnology at Kalinga University as I wanted to learn how medicine, environment, and even food can be improved through science, and I must say that my professors didn’t just give us bookish knowledge, but through lab experiments and project works, everything we studied in the classroom connected with the real-life problems.

I was able to perform in-depth research in their Pharmacy and CIF labs, and I have even published a research paper on drug formulation during my course. The constant support from my professors made me achieve my dreams.

All thanks to their dedicated faculty and placement support team, who guided me throughout my journey. I have attended workshops, visited different drug manufacturing industries, and their placement team helped me practice mock interviews. I have been placed at one of the best pharmaceutical companies in Chhattisgarh.

The Pharmacy lab at Kalinga is one of the best research and experimentation labs in Chhattisgarh. I have learned drug formulation and development, pharmacology skills, herbal drug analysis, and clinical pharmacy practices.
During my BBA LLB journey, I have learned to draft legal documents, courtroom skills, case analysis, corporate law, client counselling skills, and much more from my supportive professors.

Their Legal Aid Club inspired me to pursue human rights law, as it inspired me to support underserved communities with legal support. During my course, I have worked on real cases and also served and taught legal awareness in rural areas.

Studying LLB from Kalinga was the best decision of my life. The moot court sessions made me feel like I was practising theory in a real courtroom. Now I have learned to present my point and argue for different cases using my skills and confidence.

I have studied a Bachelor of Computer Science in artificial intelligence and machine learning from Kalinga University, and I would say that I have gained so much exposure outside the classroom as I have worked on practical projects, case studies, attended guest lectures from industry experts, and also participated in various conferences.

My experience in the Faculty of Education has been amazing. We get so many opportunities to practice real classroom teaching through micro-teaching and school visits. These practical sessions helped me improve my confidence and teaching style. The faculty always guides us step by step during these activities. I feel more prepared to become a good teacher now.

I really like the way the syllabus here is designed according to current trends and issues. We discuss real-world case studies and government policies, which makes learning very relevant. The faculty also supports us in conducting research and preparing papers for conferences. I have learnt a lot about the practical applications of political science here. It has made me more confident about my future career

Kalinga University focuses a lot on overall development, not just theory. We had cultural events, debates, seminars, and field studies that made learning very engaging. These activities helped me improve my communication and critical thinking skills. I also learnt teamwork and leadership during various group projects. The holistic approach here has shaped my personality in the best way.
